room.name: Double-height living with new loft and quarter-turn stair

elements.label: Flight 1: 7 risers along S wall, 6 treads + 1.0 x 1.0 m landing in SE corner
Flight 2: 7 risers along E wall up to loft edge
Pull-out drawers / shoe and vacuum bay under flight 2
Loft floor: steel beams + deck, top at 2.60 m, 2.40 m clear below and above
Loft edge guard 1.0 m, glass_tempered or vertical balusters < 0.10 m gaps
Open-side guard + handrail on flight 2 (sloped; boxed here)

reveal_path.line: Five metres of ceiling, half of it wasted air. Now a loft takes the back of the room.
The stair starts here, with a clear landing at its foot, and runs along the south wall.
Seven easy steps, a full landing in the corner, then a quarter turn. No winders, no ladder.
Under the second flight: drawers for shoes, the vacuum and bedding.
At the top: a loft with 2.4 m standing height and a guard along the edge.
Wide shot: stair in the open half, loft above the back, living below.

notes: Room size, door and window positions are assumed; loft depth follows from the stair.
Floor-to-loft 2.60 m = 14 risers x 0.186 m; 12 treads x 0.26 m (7.3 in riser, 10.2 in tread; IRC limits 7.75 in / 10 in). 2R+T = 0.63 m.
Headroom is open to the 5 m ceiling over both flights; the lowest point is 2.4 m at the loft arrival.
India: verify against NBC 2016 Part 3/4 and local bye-laws; IRC values used by the checker are stricter in places, looser in others.
Loft structure, anchorage into walls/slab and any FSI/permission questions need a structural engineer.
